title: SocialMediaComp — High-Reach Social Accounts Leaderboard
description: A 80-entry master list of the most-followed accounts and largest communities across seven platforms — TikTok (19), Instagram (16), Reddit (11), Facebook (5), YouTube (18), X (7) and Twitch (4) — in four cohorts (creator 36, brand 13, celebrity 20, community 11), built from Wikipedia list tables and official pages fetched in a recorded session and cross-checked row by row against the platform's own site. Every entry carries an id, platform, handle, owner, topic, metric label and value, a snapshot note, the profile URL, the source name and URL, growth notes, a verified-list flag, cohort, country, likes in billions and the batch it arrived in. The verification rule is stated in data/master-list.json itself: every follower, member or subscriber figure is taken from a cited source fetched in the session shown in docs/VERIFICATION.md, and nothing is taken from a summary that was not itself read. The repo compiles the list, flags every inconsistency it meets rather than smoothing it, and publishes a quirk register (Q1 to Q32) that includes the TikTok article's internal inconsistency over Khaby Lame's follower count, a Facebook table-ordering quirk (rank 8 Shakira 126M listed before rank 9), and cross-platform duplicates that are intentional (entries 41 and 51, MrBeast and Ronaldo, each appearing twice with different ids). data/strategies.json holds 6 keys including official_resources and a standing disclaimer that the documented patterns are platform education resources and publicly described behaviour, not growth guarantees, and that buying followers, bots or engagement pods violate platform rules. The suite was executed here: 189 tests pass (156 at the previous read). The previous version of this entry published '60 entries' and 'four batches of 15'; the list is now 80 entries in four batches of 20.
